cards.front: Which part of the cell cycle takes up most of the cell's time?
cards.back: **Interphase** takes up most of the cycle, with G1, S and G2 before division. The division phase is much shorter.
cards.hint: Compare the time spent growing and copying with the time spent splitting.

cards.front: Why does mitosis produce genetically identical daughter cells?
cards.back: Mitosis shares the **chromatids** equally between two nuclei. DNA was already copied in S phase, so both daughter nuclei get the same chromosomes and alleles as the parent.
cards.hint: Trace what happened to the DNA in S phase.

cards.front: What are the four stages of mitosis, in order?
cards.back: **Prophase**, metaphase, anaphase, telophase. Chromosomes condense and the envelope breaks down, then line up, then centromeres divide and chromatids move apart, then nuclear envelopes re-form.
cards.hint: Follow the events from the start of nuclear division to its end.

cards.front: What name is given to the long period between divisions, containing G1, S and G2?
cards.back: **Interphase**. The cell grows, copies its DNA and checks it during this period before it divides.
cards.hint: Think about what the cell does before it divides.

cards.back: One of the two identical copies of a replicated chromosome, held together at the **centromere**.
cards.hint: Consider what S phase does to each chromosome.

cards.front: Why is it wrong to say that DNA is replicated during prophase?
cards.back: DNA is replicated in the **S phase** of interphase. Chromosomes are already copied before prophase starts.

cards.front: How is the mitotic index calculated from cell counts?
cards.back: $\text{mitotic index}=\frac{\text{cells in mitosis}}{\text{total cells observed}}$. It is a ratio, so it has no units.
cards.hint: Think about what the top and bottom of the ratio count.

cards.front: A root tip squash has 120 cells observed, and 18 are in mitosis. What is the mitotic index?
cards.back: $\frac{18}{120}=0.15$, so 15% of the cells are dividing.
cards.hint: Divide the cells in mitosis by the total cells observed.

cards.front: What is the spindle in mitosis?
cards.back: A structure of **protein** fibres that moves the chromosomes during nuclear division.
cards.hint: Think about what pulls the chromatids apart.

cards.front: How does cytokinesis divide the cytoplasm differently in animal and plant cells?
cards.back: In animal cells the **cell surface membrane** pinches inwards. In plant cells a new cell wall forms across the middle.
cards.hint: Consider which cell type has a rigid outer layer.

cards.front: Where in a flowering plant does mitosis mainly take place?
cards.back: In **meristems** at the tips of roots and shoots, where they add length to the plant.
cards.hint: Think about the parts of a plant that grow longer.

cards.front: Which animal tissues show a lot of mitosis, and why?
cards.back: Tissues such as the **gut lining**, base of the skin and bone marrow. Their cells are worn away or lost often, so new cells are needed all the time.
cards.hint: Think about tissues that wear away quickly.
